correctness.rationale: Exact rational interval evaluation certifies a strictly interior fixed point and a stable two-dimensional reaction Jacobian; four opposite-sign determinant evaluations rigorously bracket exactly two positive modal thresholds. The incidence-matrix spectral comparison proves eigenvalue ratios at least ten for each normalized weighted star of arbitrary order; hence disjoint mobility intervals. A quadratic modal determinant proves the universal one-interval-per-positive-eigenvalue upper bound. No finite computation is treated as proof of the all-order bound.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Broad spectral-window theory yields a per-mode interval, but the checked source material does not prove the sharp attainable count for every graph size with one fixed physically admissible public-goods reaction and fixed mobility ratio. It remains possible that an uninspected abstract graph theorem subsumes the geometric-conductance construction.

evidence: Roy et al. supply the mode-determinant polynomial and one unstable spectral interval; their Appendix E treats its changing width rather than maximal disconnected mobility windows.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The new claim is not that a Turing band exists or that a graph may avoid it. Its conclusion quantifies the exact maximum of disconnected intervals in a one-parameter mobility sweep and attains it uniformly in graph order by a constructible conductance law; none of those implications was identified as a statement or demonstrated special case in the inspected materials.

originality.rationale: Motivating Roy et al. paper, its Appendix E, and relevant earlier graph-Turing full-text material establish the modal mechanism, but the checked statements do not give an arbitrarily long family of disconnected mobility windows on a fixed positively weighted star with fixed public-goods kinetics or the attained sharp upper bound. The result adds exact ecological calibration and all-size eigenvalue separation. Historical priority remains qualified.
residual_risks: The general two-species modal interval mechanism is classic; a broader pre-existing spectral theorem not located here could subsume the universal upper bound and graph scaling construction.

The original model used unweighted networks. Weighted positive corridor conductances are a transparent mathematical extension, so the finding does not assert that these sharp windows occur on unweighted stars.
Full-text access to some indexed neighboring mathematical results and the publisher PDF page images was unavailable; inspected summary implications do not constitute a full comparison.
This is local linear stability only and does not assert nonlinear cooperation-rich pattern existence or biological empirical relevance.

value.rationale: The sharp extremal count shows homogeneous cooperation can alternate between linear stability and instability up to twice per independent spatial mode under only one mobility knob, at fixed game and corridor configuration. This corrects the intuition that one Turing window or monotone stabilization is unavoidable, and supplies a reproducible budget-normalized family useful for understanding finite-network spectral selection. It does not claim real-world outcomes or nonlinear patterns.
